No retrieved policy covers this date, so applying PRC-2026.1 is provisional and needs review. pricing_desk is our suggested reviewer; the policy does not name one for this situation.","policy_evidence_id":"PRC-2026.1§1"}],"decision":"counter_offer","explanation":"The decision date is 2026-09-22. PRC-2026.1 covered decisions only until 2026-09-01 (exclusive), and PRC-2025.1 expired on 2026-04-01, so no retrieved policy is effective on this date. We used PRC-2026.1, the most recent policy, as a provisional basis and flagged the gap for review.

The merchant has merchant-specific cost data: 1.65% + $0.09. At volume of $650,000 and 13,000 transactions, the monthly cost is $11,895.

The merchant's requested 1.95% + $0.20 (their own unverified statement) would produce:
- Revenue: $15,275
- Gross margin: 22.13%, below the 26% mid-size minimum
- Discount vs list: 17.54%

Pricing below the minimum margin is allowed only under an approved strategic exception, which requires cfo_delegate approval. A strategic exception has been requested (sponsor: VP Partnerships), but no approval is evidenced. The claim that 'strategic pricing was promised' is also unverified. We therefore counter-offer at 2.08% + $0.20, the lowest whole-basis-point rate that meets the 26% minimum:
- Revenue: $16,120
- Gross profit: $4,225
- Gross margin: 26.21%

This is a 12.98% discount vs the mid list price of 2.45% + $0.20. That exceeds 12%, so regional_pricing_manager approval is required. Pricing at 2.11% + $0.20 or higher would keep the discount at or below 12% and avoid that approval.

No promotion applies: SPRING26 expired on 2026-06-30. Volume is far below the $4M deal_desk threshold.

If the cfo_delegate approves the strategic exception, the requested 1.95% + $0.20 could be granted.
